steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Combine baking mix, milk, and Cheddar cheese until a soft dough forms; drop by 9 spoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Combine butter and garlic powder; brush over warm biscuits.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheese-Garlic Biscuits
raw_recipe.description: This cheese-garlic biscuits recipe requires only 15 minutes and just five ingredients: baking mix, milk, butter, Cheddar cheese, and garlic powder.
raw_recipe.name: Cheese-Garlic Biscuits

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F.
Combine baking mix, milk, and Cheddar cheese until a soft dough forms; drop by 9 spoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Combine butter and garlic powder; brush over warm biscuits.

review.reviewBody: Absolutely delicious!!! They melt in your mouth. Better than Red Lobster! Changes that I made: Add extra cheese, 1/3 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 C. chopped white onions and a dash of Old Bay Seasoning (found near seafood- not in spice isle) in with the batter. Double the recipe for 4 people. Use a little garlic powder and minced garlic w/butter. I can't wait to make it again!

This is a really fast and easy recipe. These are the changes I made: I increased the amount of cheese to 1 cup, and put the garlic powder in the batter. For the topping I used equal amounts of real butter and margarine, 1/4 tsp. parsley, and about 1/8 tsp of garlic salt. Also, my family really likes the garlic flavor so I added one clove of fresh minced garlic to the mix (I use a garlic press). Also, instead of brushing the butter mixture on at the end I decided to do it while they were cooking to get better flavor... I brushed once after cooking for about 5 minutes and then again when they were almost done. It gave them a nice golden color and the flavor was amazing. If you are looking for something close to Red Lobster this is definitely the way to go.

I use granulated garlic (added directly into the raw dough) and a sharp cheddar cheese. I also like to add dill weed to the mix, either fresh or dried. If I have buttermilk on hand I will substitute some or all of the milk for extra tang.

Love it! It's a keeper. The texture of the biscuits made a perfect companion to my vegetarian chili. I read some of the alteration tips and added a pinch of garlic to the flour mix, used a mix of cheddar, gouda, and brie for the fun of it. Next time I might add some onion and parsley not because the recipe requires it but because it's fun to experiment with a solid recipe. Thank you!

Just came across this recipe this morning as a tag to an email. Such an easy recipe. Halved the biscuit mix and used a Mexican style blend cheese since I didn't have Cheddar alone. Made 5 large and 1 med. biscuits. Made the full amount of butter/garlic topping and used all of it on the 6 biscuits. Tasted great and took about five minutes to put together.

What a great way to get those restaurant style biscuits at home! These were indeed very close to the dine-in place's. I always have biscuit mix on hand, butter is a staple, along with cheese, so these were a zero cost item to make. I did add a bit of parsley to the melted butter/garlic mix. I did have to add a bit more milk as these were too dense for me. These were not as tender or moist as the restaurant ones, but they did what I needed, and I didn't have to spend $80 to dine out. I've got a better recipe, but in a pinch, this was just fine.

These biscuits were not up to Onion John standards! According to Onion John, these biscuits do not have the required ingredients of 4 tablespoons of butter and 1/2 a teaspoon of garlic powder. I am very disappointed of whoever wrote this article. Onion John would be disappointed!

This is a good building block recipe. I was looking for a tasty biscuit recipe using Bisquick. Unfortunately, I had run out of cheese and had about 1 pat of butter left. So, scouring my cupboards, I found a packet of chicken flavor ramen seasoning. I added that packet to the biscuit mixture, baked as directed. When out of the oven, I put slivers of butter on top to melt (omitting the garlic powder). Really quite good. I did not miss the cheese at all. I will experiment with this recipe.
These were great!!! I did make some changes... I added 1/3 garlic powder to the mix before baking them, doubled the cheese and added 1/4 cup dried parsley to the mix as well!!!
This is pretty much the first thing I have ever tried to make.Very easy,and my boyfriend loved them!! I doubled the cheese and added 1/3 tsp garlic to the batter before I cooked it.

i made a huge batch of these for a party that i served pasta at and they were a hit! the only thing i added was some garlic powder to the batter and did half and half garlic powder and garlic salt to the melted butter portion. they were very easy to make and taste way better than Red Lobster's rolls.
Delicious biscuits, baked for 15 minutes and they are perfect.
Simple and delicious! Great quick addition to dinner!
Delicious, I did use a cup of cheese and they turned out so yummy!
Added a dash of sweet cream.
This is a very quick biscuit with a delicate flavor of garlic. This is a good recipe to bake up when you may need bread in a pinch.
Needed seasoning....like garlic powder, onion powder, red pepper flakes. Was alright but needed elevation. Was doughy in the center.
Love these! Perfectly, mouth wateringly tasty.
Love these cheesy biscuits. Simply and delicious.
Wow! Tastes exactly like red lobsters biscuits. Will make again!
